clue.text: Skill put over by bridge partners wanting manuscript changes

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting a word over turns it back to front

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
North and South are partners at the bridge table
wanting, as in keen on, is for (all for it)

explanation.surface: A card player's knack, shown off by bridge partners who need to amend a handwritten document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' reverses the skill word. 'wanting' is FOR in the sense of all for something; North and South always partner each other at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs in the third person: something that changes another thing alters its form.

indicators.note: the hospital letter sits inside the word for the tower

parts.note: a tug is a boat that tows other vessels, so a tower
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A violent man is locked up in a hospital inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' reads as a tall building but means something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both name a violent, brutish person.

clue.text: Diplomat, teetotal, entering suitable organisation? Revolutionary

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, entering it

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, AA, is the organisation suited to someone who is teetotal
Che Guevara is the classic revolutionary

explanation.surface: A sober diplomat joins a fitting body, then turns out to be a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal but is Che Guevara; the question mark flags AA as a jokey 'suitable organisation' for a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior member of an embassy staff, a kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Dealer in quarrel over chart men ruined

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of chart men are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A trader quarrels over a chart that has spoiled his staff's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who buys and sells old metal and junk is a kind of dealer.

clue.text: Operation on spasm with Scotsman seeing doctor

parts.note: a tic is a twitching spasm
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scotsman

explanation.surface: After an operation, a Scot with a twitch goes to see the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing doctor' reads as a visit, but it is a doctor of seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist deals with sight, so is a doctor for seeing, loosely.

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of moans are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: A labourer complains bitterly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker builds with his hands, so is a manual worker.

parts.note: dos are parties or social gatherings
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Is it hard to change one's partying habits?
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' is coins, and DOSH is British slang for money; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money; loose coins are one example of it.

parts.note: over can mean about or on account of, as in a row over money
a run is a race

explanation.surface: An army attacks because of an ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to swarm into and occupy territory.

clue.text: Easily riled, like a dinosaur? Anything but!

definitions.meaning: dinosaurs, as reptiles, were thought cold-blooded, so the opposite is warm-blooded

explanation.walkthrough: Reptiles are cold-blooded, so 'anything but' like a dinosaur gives the opposite temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-blooded is an idiom for passionate and quick-tempered.

definitions.meaning: to say or voice a word
complete or absolute, as in an absolute fool

explanation.definitionFit: One verb meaning to say, one adjective meaning total, sharing the same spelling.

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

indicators.note: playing means the letters of meant are moving about

explanation.surface: An international match was supposed to be played as a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges MEANT into AMENT. A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a solemn statement or proof, so a declaration.

clue.text: Pre-Christmas period restricts Queen broadcast times, becoming commercial

indicators.note: the outer word restricts, hems in, the inner pieces

parts.note: Advent is the season leading up to Christmas
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: broadcast, scattered, means the letters of times are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advent schedules squeeze the Queen's broadcast times as it all becomes commercialised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the Queen's Christmas speech, but it is the anagram signal; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial is a TV or radio advert promoting a product.

clue.text: Head may maintain a large place to fire 13

parts.note: a cape is a headland
may and can both express being allowed
to aver is to assert or maintain
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A boss may keep a big site for firing things.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points at the answer to 13 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida launch site from which NASA sends rockets into orbit.

clue.text: Art room first to show heavenly vehicle

indicators.note: first places the word for room ahead of the word for art

parts.note: space is room, as in no room to move
craft is skill or art

explanation.surface: A gallery space must first show art before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that travels through the heavens, beyond Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Quietly belie running article that's working-class

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of belie are in motion and rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A quietly running piece that belies its working-class roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means of the common people, the lower orders.

parts.note: a make is a brand of product
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Win an Oscar for an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlon Brando, the actor, did win Oscars, which makes 'Oscar' a lovely decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was a celebrated American film star.

clue.text: Save theatre with regularly praised view

parts.note: rep, repertory, is a kind of theatre

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of praised view

explanation.surface: Rescue a theatre that has had consistently good reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a stay of execution to; to spare or rescue from a fate.

clue.text: Risk part of church getting left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble that part of a church will be overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun: a chance or a risk is a possibility of something happening.

definitions.meaning: baffled, not knowing what to do
a profit below zero is a deficit, so trading in the red

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means puzzled, and literally describes selling for less than cost.

clue.text: Indifferent physician hiding nothing with note

indicators.note: the word for physician hides, holds within it, the letter for nothing

parts.note: a medic is a doctor or physician
O is zero, nothing
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An uncaring doctor conceals nothing in his note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indifferent' here means not very good, not uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent in its sense of ordinary, of only average quality.

indicators.note: the rogue goes inside the word for lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a scoundrel or rogue

explanation.surface: The downfall of a scoundrel caught up in a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, a fall of water.

definitions.meaning: with no letters, read literally as having no written symbols

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlettered' usually means illiterate; here it means literally without letters, that is without characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Character means both a written symbol and personality, so having none fits both.

clue.text: Teach fool the wrong way to describe artists

indicators.note: to describe is to draw a line round, so the reversed fool encloses the artists
the wrong way means the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: a nit, nitwit, is a fool
RA, Royal Academician, stands for artists

explanation.surface: Trying to instruct an idiot to sketch painters, getting it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' makes NIT into TIN; 'describe' is used in its geometric sense, to draw around.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to coach or instruct someone.

definitions.meaning: a regular route or patrol, as a police officer's

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a police officer's route and a verb meaning to hit repeatedly.

indicators.note: after puts the word for confront behind a fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing
to face is to confront

explanation.surface: Confronting someone after a fight, then backing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete change of direction or opinion, a U-turn.

indicators.note: admits means the words Luke and Vader let in, contain, the letters

explanation.surface: A Star Wars villain confesses he tells Luke to keep away.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to dodge or keep clear of.

indicators.note: rebuffed, pushed back, means the words for son and boozer are read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A timid son gets rejected by a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is the verb to throw, as in a coconut shy, not timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to throw or fling.

definitions.meaning: stocks and shares are examples of money put to work
a vicar is dressed in robes, so split as in robes

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN VESTMENT: a vicar wears vestments, priestly robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are one example of putting money into something for a return.
